theme.title: The Lost Melody Islands
theme.subtitle: Quest for the Hidden Treasure
theme.intro:
The Story Begins

Lyra Explorer Choon Music Robot

Every adventure needs a team! Lyra is a fearless explorer, and Choon is her cheerful music robot who can hear melodies hidden everywhere.

The magical Grand Melody that once connected all the islands has disappeared. Its pieces are scattered across the sea. Solve musical puzzles, discover hidden melodies, and help your new friends restore the song before the islands fall silent forever.

echo_island.label: Echo Island Guardian
echo_island.message: Big Badge unlocked: Echo Island Guardian. The island can hear music again!

harmony_geometry_reef.label: Geometry Reef Navigator
harmony_geometry_reef.message: Big Badge unlocked: Geometry Reef Navigator. Lyra can now read the reef's shape-rhythm map!

broadcast_bay.label: Broadcast Bay Signalkeeper
broadcast_bay.message: Big Badge unlocked: Broadcast Bay Signalkeeper. Every mouse in the bay answers its own call now!

starlight_summit.label: Keeper of the Grand Melody
starlight_summit.message: Big Badge unlocked: Keeper of the Grand Melody. The song that once joined every island is whole again.

pulse_lighthouse.label: Pulse Lighthouse Keeper
pulse_lighthouse.message: Big Badge unlocked: Pulse Lighthouse Keeper. The beacon turns in perfect time, and every island can find its way home again.

singing_stones.label: Singing Stones Keeper
singing_stones.message: Big Badge unlocked: Singing Stones Keeper. The whole shore answers your touch, and the last of the Grand Melody comes home.

problems.title: The Bridge of Echo Island
problems.description:
Lyra and Choon step onto Echo Island. The bridge is gone, but the sea is still humming. Choon points to an old song-map carved in stone.

A A B A

"These marks are sounds," Choon whispers. "If we hear them first, we can wake the bridge."

Bridge Song

Try playing the loose A and B chunks. When their sounds feel familiar, place them under Start to match the song-map above.

Press Play. If the bridge starts to glow, press Check My Work.

Secret Paths

After the bridge rises, try one small change. The island may answer.

makeLonger.title: Make it longer
makeLonger.heading: Make the sound last longer
makeLonger.description:
You can make a tone or path longer by adding another action chunk after the song, repeating a favorite chunk, or placing more notes inside an action before you play it again.
Musically, this gives the melody more time to travel without changing the main idea.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The first path begins where echoes answer twice.

badges.label: Bridge Builder
badges.message: The stone tablet begins to glow. Music echoes across the island, and a shining bridge slowly rises from the ocean.

badges.label: Name Keeper
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Name Keeper. Lyra labels the music map in her own explorer style.

badges.label: Sky Builder
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Sky Builder. The bridge stretches higher into the clouds.

badges.label: Melody Shifter
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Melody Shifter. The bridge glows with a new color.

badges.label: Secret Treasure Coin
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. You discovered a path Captain Cadence never recorded.

problems.title: The Sakura Grove Echo
problems.description:
Across the new bridge, Lyra and Choon find a silent Sakura grove. A journal page flutters from one branch: "Sing the old blossom melody, and the petals will show the next clue."

#2

Choon hears four sleepy chunks from Sakura Sakura. Play them once, then guide them along the petal trail.

Petal Song

Sakura yayoi miwatasu yayoi miwatasu Sakura miniyukan

Place the chunks under Start in the trail shown above. Let the trail bloom 4 times, press Play, then check the grove.

Hidden Petals

When the trees answer, try one new twist. Some petals hide secret badges.

makeLonger.title: Make a longer path
makeLonger.heading: Extend the petal trail
makeLonger.description:
You can make the path longer by adding another action chunk, repeating a favorite Sakura chunk, or placing more notes inside an action before you use it again.
Musically, a longer path gives the melody more time to bloom while the pattern still feels connected.

rewards: Treasure Clue: Follow the petals when the old grove sings four times.

badges.label: Sakura Echo
badges.message: The Sakura trees begin to sing. Petals swirl into the air and reveal Captain Cadence's next journal page.

badges.label: Grove Name Keeper
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Grove Name Keeper. Lyra adds her own names to the Sakura map.

badges.label: Petal Lifter
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Petal Lifter. The blossoms float higher as the melody climbs.

badges.label: Grove Shifter
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Grove Shifter. The Sakura grove glows with a new color.

badges.label: Petal Trail Coin
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. Your longer Sakura path reveals petals Captain Cadence never followed.

problems.title: The Pulse Cave Rhythm
problems.description:
Past the Sakura grove, Lyra and Choon hear a soft tapping inside a blue cave. The treasure map is quiet, but the cave walls blink like a heartbeat.

#3

"This clue is not a melody first," Choon says. "It is a pulse. We need to build the beat before the next song can wake up."

Pulse Cave Beat

Open Rhythm Maker. Create a steady beat, try a few long and short rhythm changes, then click Save rhythms.

Find the exported rhythm action in the Action palette, place it under Start, press Play, and listen for the cave's heartbeat.

Secret Beats

After the cave starts blinking, try a rhythm experiment. These discoveries are about beat, length, and drum color.

saveRhythm.title: Save rhythms
saveRhythm.heading: Turn your beat into a chunk
saveRhythm.description:
Use Rhythm Maker to shape the pulse, then press Save rhythms. Music Blocks creates a new action called rhythm. Put that action under Start so your program can play it.
Musically, exporting turns your rhythm idea into a reusable pattern.

changeLength.title: Change note lengths
changeLength.heading: Stretch or shorten the beat
changeLength.description:
Open Rhythm Maker and change one rhythm value so the pulse is no longer all the same length. Try changing the rhythm from 1/1 to 1/2, 1/4, or another value, then listen again.
This unlocks the Beat Shaper discovery because longer and shorter notes change the rhythm pattern while the beat keeps moving.

drumMachine.title: Save drum machine
drumMachine.heading: Make the cave answer with drums
drumMachine.description: After trying a rhythm, press Save drum machine in Rhythm Maker. This creates an action that plays drum sounds directly. Use it when you want the beat to sound like a percussion pattern, not just a rhythm guide.

incomplete.title: The Pulse Cave Is Still Quiet
incomplete.message: Choon hears the beat in Rhythm Maker, but Start is not playing the exported rhythm yet. Click Save rhythms, find the rhythm action, place it under Start, then press Check My Work.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The next path opens when a steady pulse carries a changing rhythm.

badges.label: Pulse Cave Keeper
badges.message: The cave lights blink in time. Lyra and Choon save the rhythm path in Captain Cadence's journal.

badges.label: Beat Shaper
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Beat Shaper. The cave pulse stretches and snaps as your notes become longer and shorter.

badges.label: Drum Taster
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Drum Taster. A new drum color echoes from the cave wall.

badges.label: Drum Machine Builder
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Drum Machine Builder. The cave answers with a full percussion pattern.

problems.title: Chest, Snap, Clap - Build the Rhythm
problems.description:
The Pulse Cave opens onto a bright stone cove. Three carvings glow on the sand: chest, snap, and clap. Choon taps the pattern on his metal shell, and the rocks answer back.

Chest Snap Clap
#4

"This rhythm has two halves," Lyra says. "If we map the body sounds over time, the cove can show the next treasure mark."

Body Beat Map

This is the rhythm the cove is tapping. Say it out loud with Choon first, one body sound for every box.

Half 1
ChestClapSnapClap
ChestClapSnapClap
Half 2
ChestClapSnapClap
ChestClapSnapClapClap

Both halves are the same until the very last box. There the single clap becomes two quick claps in the same amount of time, so the rhythm runs straight on into the next round. Musicians call that quick pair two sixteenth notes.

Open Phrase Maker and give each body sound its own drum row. Tap the boxes so the drums play in that order, then save Half 1 as an action chunk. Build Half 2 the same way.

Put both chunks under Start, wrap them in a repeat block, and press Play. The cove should clap back.

Secret Body Beats

Once the cove starts clapping back, try a body-rhythm twist. These discoveries are about form, loops, sound choices, and remixing.

exportHalves.title: Export two halves
exportHalves.heading: Make two rhythm chunks
exportHalves.description:
Use Phrase Maker to build the first half, then save it as an action. Build the second half with its shorter sixteenth-note ending and save that too. Place both action chunks under Start.
Musically, two chunks make a call-and-answer shape: the first half sets the pattern, and the second half changes the ending.

loopGroove.title: Loop the groove
loopGroove.heading: Make the body beat repeat
loopGroove.description:
Put a repeat block under Start and place both Phrase Maker action chunks inside it. Try repeating the full groove 2 or 4 times.
This unlocks the Loop Leader discovery because a rhythm becomes easier to feel when it comes around again.

swapBodySounds.title: Swap body sounds
swapBodySounds.heading: Change the cove's body sounds
swapBodySounds.description:
Click a drum name inside your Phrase Maker action and choose a different sound from the pie menu. For example, replace one drum with a bell, clap, or another percussion sound.
Musically, the timing stays the same, but the color of the rhythm changes.

remixGroove.title: Make your own groove
remixGroove.heading: Add one extra body-beat idea
remixGroove.description:
After your two-part rhythm works, add another exported Phrase Maker action or call one of your actions one more time under Start.
This unlocks the Cove Remixer discovery because you are extending the form beyond the required rhythm.

incomplete.title: The Body Beat Cove Is Waiting
incomplete.message: Choon hears some taps, but the cove needs two Phrase Maker action chunks under Start, looped with a repeat block. Export both halves, place both actions in the loop, then check again.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The treasure door listens for two body-beat answers inside one loop.

badges.label: Body Beat Builder
badges.message: The cove claps back in two parts. Lyra records the body rhythm in Captain Cadence's journal.

badges.label: Two-Part Mapper
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Two-Part Mapper. Your first half and second half answer each other clearly.

badges.label: Loop Leader
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Loop Leader. The body beat circles around until everyone can feel the groove.

badges.label: Body Sound Designer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Body Sound Designer. The same rhythm speaks with a new sound color.

badges.label: Cove Remixer
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. Your extra body-beat idea makes the cove dance in a new way.

problems.title: The Shape Drum Reef
problems.description:
After the Body Beat Cove claps back, Captain Cadence's map folds into three glowing outlines. Choon hears each shape like a rhythm: one whole circle split into equal beats.

#5

"A full turn is 360 degrees," Choon says. "Split the turn into sides, and the turtle draws the rhythm of a shape."

Shape Rhythm

Use the loose repeat, forward, and right blocks to draw a square: repeat 4, forward 100, right 90.

Then duplicate the idea to keep three separate Start programs: a triangle, a square, and a pentagon.

Hidden Shape Beats

When the three shapes appear, try one deeper geometry trick. The reef hides badges in math, color, and new polygons.

extraPolygon.title: Make another shape
extraPolygon.heading: Try a new split of the circle
extraPolygon.description:
After triangle, square, and pentagon work, duplicate one Start program and change the repeat number and turn angle for another polygon. For example, 6 sides turns by 60 degrees because 360 divided by 6 is 60.
This unlocks the Polygon Explorer discovery because you used the same whole-circle idea beyond the required shapes.

incomplete.title: The Shape Reef Is Still Faint
incomplete.message: Choon sees part of the reef, but it needs three separate Start programs: triangle, square, and pentagon. Each one should use repeat, forward, and right with the correct turn.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The Heart of Harmony listens for circles split into equal shape beats.

badges.label: Shape Reef Builder
badges.message: The reef lights up with triangle, square, and pentagon rhythms. Lyra saves the shape clue in Captain Cadence's journal.

badges.label: Circle Divider
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Circle Divider. You split 360 degrees like a whole note divided into beats.

badges.label: Box Geometer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Box Geometer. One stored number now guides the shape's repeat and turn.

badges.label: Reef Colorist
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Reef Colorist. The geometry reef glows with a new color.

badges.label: Polygon Explorer
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. You drew a new shape Captain Cadence did not mark on the reef.

problems.title: The Spinning Polyrhythm Lagoon
problems.description:
Beyond the Shape Drum Reef, Lyra finds a lagoon where two ripples dance at once. One ripple taps in 2. The other taps in 3. Choon whispers, "That is a polyrhythm: two rhythms moving together, meeting, and separating."

2
3
#6

Captain Cadence's page says: "When the beats move differently, let an avatar show the motion so your eyes can hear the rhythm too."

Lagoon Mission

Use the two rhythm rulers on the screen: keep one as a duplet rhythm and one as a triplet rhythm. Then connect an avatar and an on every note do action so the music makes something move.

Press Play and listen for the moment when the 2-beat ripple and the 3-beat ripple meet again.

Hidden Ripple Tricks

The lagoon has extra marks for explorers who make the rhythm visible in new ways.

noteMotion.title: Note-value motion
noteMotion.heading: Let notes control movement
noteMotion.description: Use a mouse note value or mouse notes played block inside the animation action. A short note can make a small turn, and a longer note can make a bigger turn. This helps the avatar show the rhythm instead of only playing it.

incomplete.title: The Lagoon Is Still Quiet
incomplete.message: Choon hears the 2-beat and 3-beat ripples, but the lagoon also needs animation. Connect an on every note do action and an avatar so the rhythm makes motion on the screen.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The Heart of Harmony appears when different beats move together without losing their own path.

badges.label: Lagoon Conductor
badges.message: The duplet and triplet ripples begin to spin together. Lyra adds the lagoon's moving rhythm to Captain Cadence's journal.

badges.label: Extra Ripple Maker
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Extra Ripple Maker. You added a rhythm ripple beyond the lagoon's 2 and 3 pattern.

badges.label: Avatar Spark
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Avatar Spark. The lagoon has a performer now.

badges.label: Note Motion Mapper
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Note Motion Mapper. Your animation listens to note values, just like Captain Cadence hinted.

badges.label: Singing Ripple
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Singing Ripple. You added a pitched voice to the moving rhythm.

badges.label: Spin Choreographer
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. Your avatar turns with the rhythm and shows the lagoon's phase shift.

problems.title: The Conductor's Signal Ring
problems.description:
The spinning lagoon carries Lyra and Choon into Broadcast Bay. Twelve small drum mice sit in a wide circle holding their drums, and not one of them makes a sound. "They cannot feel the beat," Choon says. "Each mouse is waiting to hear its own name."

#7

In the middle stands Mr. Mouse, the conductor. Captain Cadence's page says: "One caller, many listeners. Send a name into the air, and only the mouse who owns that name will answer."

Two Tricks for the Ring

Adding words. The plus (+) block adds numbers, but it can also stick words together. "event" + "5" becomes event5. That is how one broadcast can call a different mouse every time around.

Counting in a circle. The mod block counts and then starts over. Mod 12 only ever gives 0, 1, 2 ... 11, and then goes back to 0. It works like counting beats in a measure, except the ring starts at 0 instead of 1.

Ring Mission

The two action chunks on the canvas already belong to the drum mice, and the loose blocks beside them are your ingredients. Your job is to wake up the conductor.

  1. Snap the forever loop under Mr. Mouse's Start block, then put the arc block inside it so the conductor keeps walking around the ring.
  2. Add a broadcast whose name is built by the plus (+) block, so it calls event0, event1, event2, and onward.
  3. Use the mod block so the count wraps back to 0 after 11 and the conductor never runs out of mice to call.
  4. Keep the mouse setup chunk, which uses listen and setxy so each drum mouse jumps into the ring when it hears its name.

Press Play, then click a drum mouse to change the sound it answers with.

Think About

  • What does broadcast mean outside of computers? Who listens?
  • How is Mr. Mouse like a conductor counting 1, 2, 3 around a circle of drummers?
  • Why can mod 12 never reach 12?
  • What would happen if two mice listened for the same name?

Hidden Signals

The bay keeps marks for explorers who make the ring bigger, louder, or more alive.

makeMice.title: Make the ring of mice
makeMice.heading: Give every drum its own mouse
makeMice.description:
Every drum in the ring is its own mouse, so every drum needs its own Start block. Add a Start block, use a set name block to call it 0, and then call the mouse setup chunk so it listens for event0. Add another Start named 1, then 2, and keep going.
Twelve mice give you twelve beats, but three or four are already enough to hear the ring turn.

toggleTrick.title: Switch 1 and 0
toggleTrick.heading: One number that flips itself
toggleTrick.description:
Inside the change action, store in the box the value 1 minus the box. If the box holds 0, then 1 - 0 = 1. If the box holds 1, then 1 - 1 = 0, so the number flips every time the mouse is clicked.
Musically, that single number chooses which of two drums the mouse answers with.

incomplete.title: The Ring Is Still Silent
incomplete.message: Choon can see the mice, but nobody is calling them. The conductor needs an arc inside a loop, a broadcast whose name is built with the plus (+) block, and a mod block so the count wraps back to 0. Keep the mouse setup chunk with its listen and setxy blocks.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The last door opens where one voice calls and many answer, each in its turn.

badges.label: Ring Conductor
badges.message: Mr. Mouse calls a name, a drum mouse answers, and the ring begins to turn. Lyra copies the signal circle into Captain Cadence's journal.

badges.label: Toggle Trickster
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Toggle Trickster. One small subtraction now flips a drum between two sounds.

badges.label: Ring Drummer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Ring Drummer. Broadcast Bay finally hears the beat it was waiting for.

badges.label: Mouse Ringmaker
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Mouse Ringmaker. Your ring has enough mice to pass the beat all the way around.

badges.label: Box Reader
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Box Reader. The conductor can look inside a box and learn which drum to call for.

badges.label: Ring Dancer
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. The drum mice do not only play now, they dance when their name is called.

problems.title: The Starlight Sky Song

journal.title: Starlight Sky Song
learned: Song form A1 A2 B B A1 A2

problems.description:
The signal ring's last call swings open the door at the top of the world. Beyond it Lyra and Choon climb to Starlight Summit, where the Grand Melody was first sung. The sky above is dark. "The stars went quiet when the song was lost," Choon says. "Sing them back and they will shine."

LaSolFa MiReDo
#8

Every star sits at its own height. A star low in the sky is a low note, and a star high in the sky is a high note. Reading left to right is reading forward in time. That is pitch over time, and the stars above spell the first phrase of the star song.

The Star Song

Sing it once before you build it, so your ears know where it goes. Twinkle Twinkle has three phrases:

  • A1: Do Do Sol Sol La La Sol
  • A2: Fa Fa Mi Mi Re Re Do
  • B: Sol Sol Fa Fa Mi Mi Re

Every pitch uses octave 4, and Phrase Maker's rhythm already fits: six short notes and one long one, exactly seven stars per phrase.

Summit Mission

Phrase Maker is already set up with Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol and La. You only need to place the stars.

  1. Click the Phrase Maker block to open the grid, then click squares to build phrase A1.
  2. Press Save to turn that phrase into an action block, then build and save A2 and B the same way.
  3. Find your three saved actions in the Actions palette and stack them under Start in song order: A1 A2 B B A1 A2.
  4. Press Play. If it sounds like the star song, the sky lights up.

Choon's trick for remembering the order: it is a sandwich. The two A phrases are the bread on the outside, and B is the peanut butter and jelly in the middle.

Think About

  • Which part of the song climbs, and which part comes back down?
  • Why does the B phrase get played twice in the middle?
  • If a star moved one row higher, would the song sound higher or lower there?

Hidden Starlight

The summit keeps marks for explorers who make the star song their own.

exportParts.title: Save each part
exportParts.heading: Turn one phrase into an action block
exportParts.description:
When a phrase looks right in the Phrase Maker grid, press the Save button on the widget. Music Blocks builds a new action block named action, then action1, then action2 for the ones after it, and they appear in the Actions palette.
Musically, each saved action is one phrase of the song that you can play back whenever you want.

sandwichForm.title: Sandwich form
sandwichForm.heading: Bread outside, peanut butter inside
sandwichForm.description:
Stack your saved actions under Start in this order: A1, A2, B, B, A1, A2. The two A phrases are the bread on the outside of the sandwich, and the B phrase in the middle is the peanut butter and jelly.
Musically, coming back to the A phrases at the end is what makes a song feel finished.

incomplete.title: The Stars Are Still Dim
incomplete.message: Choon hears part of the star song. Phrase Maker needs all three phrases saved as action blocks - Do Do Sol Sol La La Sol, then Fa Fa Mi Mi Re Re Do, then Sol Sol Fa Fa Mi Mi Re - and those actions stacked under Start as A1 A2 B B A1 A2.

rewards: Treasure Found: The Grand Melody is whole again, and every island you woke up sings it back.

badges.label: Star Song Keeper
badges.message: Star by star the summit lights up, and the Grand Melody returns. Lyra writes the last page of Captain Cadence's journal.

badges.label: Sandwich Namer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Sandwich Namer. Your phrases have names you chose, so the form reads like a recipe.

badges.label: High Star
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: High Star. One note now shines from a different octave.

badges.label: Star Variation
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Star Variation. You moved the whole song to a new place, the way Mozart did with this very tune.

badges.label: Star Dancer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Star Dancer. The mouse turns with the melody and draws the sky as it sings.

badges.label: Second Voice
badges.message: Secret Treasure Coin found. A second Start block joins in, and the star song has harmony.

problems.title: The Pulse Lighthouse
problems.description:
Past the summit the sea turns dark. A lighthouse stands there with its great lamp still, because the keeper who counted its turns is long gone. "Every island set its clocks by that light," says Choon. "Give it a heartbeat and it will wake."

Lyra puts a hand on her chest and feels her own pulse: one, two, one, two. "That is what the lamp needs," she says. "A beat that never wanders."

Tick and Tock

Beat 1 - low drum Beat 2 - bright drum

A Forever block is already turning on your canvas with one drum inside it. Add a second note value drum and give it a different drum sound, so the lamp ticks and tocks instead of repeating itself. Press Play, then check the lighthouse.

Hidden Gears

Once the lamp is turning, try one new gear. Each one hides a badge.

colorBeat.title: Color every beat
colorBeat.heading: Paint the light with the beat count
colorBeat.description:
Once a Meter block is counting, the Beat Count block reports which beat you are on. Drop Beat Count into Set Color and the lamp changes colour on every beat.
Multiply it first if the colours look too alike, because the colour scale runs from 0 to 100.
colorBeat.musicDescription: Hearing the beat and seeing it at the same time makes the difference between beat and rhythm much easier to feel.

rewards: Treasure Clue: The light keeps time for every island at once.

badges.label: Beacon Keeper
badges.message: Tick, tock. The great lamp turns with your beat and a beam sweeps out across the water.

badges.label: Pendulum Swinger
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Pendulum Swinger. Choon leans left and right with the beat, exactly like a real metronome.

badges.label: Tempo Master
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Tempo Master. The beacon can race like a running heart or rest like a sleeping one.

badges.label: Meter Marker
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Meter Marker. Lyra writes how many beats and what kind, and the lamp starts counting in measures.

badges.label: Beat Painter
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Beat Painter. The beam changes colour on every beat, so you can see the pulse as well as hear it.

incomplete.title: The Lamp Still Sleeps
incomplete.message: Choon hears one drum going round and round, but a metronome needs two different sounds to tick and tock. Add another note value drum inside the Forever block and give it a different drum, then press Check My Work.

problems.title: The Singing Stones
problems.description:
On the last shore, a row of tall stones stands in the sand. Lyra taps one and nothing happens. "They are not broken," says Choon. "They are waiting. A stone like this only sings when someone touches it, and somebody has to tell it what to sing."

On a real piano a key pushes a hammer, the hammer strikes a string, and the string sings. Here a click is the hammer, and the note you choose is the string.

Two Stones, Two Voices

Key 1 - sol (already built for you) Key 2 - a note of your own

One stone already works. Its mouse listens with on click do, and the matching action plays sol. Copy the Start and action blocks to build a second key with its own note, press Play, then click your stones.

Hidden Voices

Once two stones answer you, try one new idea. Each one hides a badge.
rewards: Treasure Clue: A stone answers only the hand that touches it.

badges.label: Stone Singer
badges.message: You touch the first stone and it sings, then the second answers in a different voice. The shore has a piano again.

badges.label: Key Namer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Key Namer. Every stone knows its own name now, so Lyra can call any of them.

badges.label: Key Spacer
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Key Spacer. The stones stand apart along the sand, so your hand never hits two at once.

badges.label: Drum Key
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Drum Key. A stone answers with a drum beneath its note, and the sand shakes a little.

badges.label: Face of the Stone
badges.message: Hidden Discovery: Face of the Stone. Each key wears a face of its own, and the shore looks back at you.

incomplete.title: The Stones Stay Quiet
incomplete.message: Choon hears one stone answer your hand, but a piano needs more than one key. Copy the Start and action blocks to build a second key with its own note, then press Check My Work.
